evidence.requirements: Almost every point in the brief is met. The start page has the heading, the Search field, the Family select (All plus 5 families) and a live '<n> cartridges' count (app.js:34-74, list.jpg). Detail facts follow the brief's order, with the water capacity source link (app.js:128-138). Tables grouped by section have Symbol/Value/Unit columns, and each tolerance sits next to its value ('39.62 -0.2', 'R 1.4 -0.25' in detail-308_win.jpg and detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). Print button, 'All cartridges' link and hash addresses are in place (app.js:124-127,158-171). The SVG is 1 unit = 1 mm with aria-label '<name> drawing', a dash-dot centre line, a hatched section and a title block with name, table, revision, 'Dimensions in mm' and scale. Rule 9 notes list missing values. Partly met: (1) the shoulder angle α gets only a single-arrow leader with a label (drawing.js:242-247, README 'leader with arrowhead'), not a dimension with extension lines; (2) in print, the drawing is capped by max-height 140mm (style.css:155), so the outline fills about 75% of the page width rather than the full width (print-308_win.jpg); (3) the scale in the title block is only the A4 print scale ('Scale 2.0 : 1 (A4 print)'), not the scale on screen.
evidence.correctness: geometry.js follows the rules closely. Rim type uses the R1/P1 thresholds (18-29). The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (202-206). The rimfire half-round has ρ=min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) (192-200). The groove floor to E1/2 + e min then ramps to (P1/2,E). The belt ramp is dz = dr/tanδ to R3/2, then runs to E and steps in (226-251). The shoulder runs through (P2/2,L1)-(H1/2,L2) with r1 min/r2 fillets (272-282). Seating and k factors are tabled exactly (67-72). The tangent ogive centre is at G1/2-ρ and ends exactly at m/2. The ellipse and cone noses are correct. The heeled 22 LR uses H2 outside and H2-2tb for the heel (147-150). Walls use tn/tb, with w the maximum of the brief's terms. Pocket sizes match the rule (61-65). Against the references, proportions look true: on 308 Win. the length-to-diameter ratio is about 5.9 against about 6.0 in reference/308_win.png. The 300 Win. Mag. belt, the 9,3 x 74 R shallow 10°58' shoulder and the 22 LR half-round rim all show correctly in the screenshots. Values come straight from the data and DMS angles render as 71°25'59". The print is one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). Weaknesses: α is not drawn as an angle dimension. Straight-case walls blend tb→tn up to the bullet base, an interpretation that is documented in the README.
evidence.security: All DOM built from data goes through the h() helper with textContent (app.js:10-29). The only innerHTML is the SVG string (app.js:117). In it, text and the name are escaped by esc() (drawing.js:15-17,123,288,302) and numbers pass through n(). rec.key is interpolated unescaped into the pattern id (drawing.js:301,308). It is trusted [a-z0-9_] data, but strictly it is unescaped data. There is no eval, no fetch and no external resource. The e2e test asserts no non-file requests (e2e.test.js:44,116).
evidence.code_quality: There are small, clearly separated UMD modules: format, catalog, geometry (pure) and drawing, plus the app router. Naming follows the brief's symbols, and missing values are reported through notes instead of exceptions. Weak points: drawing.js layout() is a single ~250-line function with many magic factors (0.58·fs, 1.9·fs and so on) and terse names (gSec, it.y0, s0/r0). It also contains a DFS label packer with iterative deepening. The code is old-style ES5 with var throughout.
evidence.tests: There are 4 unit files (node:test) and an e2e suite (playwright-core). Geometry tests check each drawing rule against the records: rim types including synthetic rebated and rimmed cases, chamfer points, groove, belt ramp at δ, rimfire half-round, shoulder fillets, every bullet shape's s/k/m, the ogive radius, the heel, the walls, w, pocket sizes and rule-9 notes for deleted values (geometry.test.js). Drawing tests check the required labels with values, the DMS α, true scale, arrows and extension lines for every dimension, and no label overlap across all 25 records (drawing.test.js:99-113). E2E covers search, filter, the detail page, reload, 404, label overlap with real font metrics, phone width, dark mode, print to PDF on one A4 page for all 25 records, and a static server. Not tested: α/2 cone slope and fillet radii.
evidence.ux_design: The page is dense and calm. A facts grid sits above the drawing and four-column Symbol/Value/Unit tables follow, with right-aligned tabular numbers (detail-308_win.jpg). Drawing labels are large and do not overlap, and the title block is clear. The drawing figure leaves wide empty margins on desktop, because max-height 80vh lets height bound the SVG (detail-300_win_mag.jpg). The diameter lines for R1, E1 and P1 crowd the head area. The print layout is legible and compact, with a footer, but the drawing could be larger and about an eighth of the page is left blank at the bottom (print-308_win.jpg). There is no dark-mode screenshot; the CSS variables support it (style.css:19-34).
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, an aria-label and a <title> (drawing.js:305-307). Tables have captions and th scope col/row (app.js:66-71,98-106). Search and Family have real <label for> elements, the count is role=status, and there is a skip link. Focus moves to main on route change (app.js:167), :focus-visible is styled, and the text colours have good contrast (#55606b on #f6f7f8). The drawing's text alternative is only its name, with no summary of the main dimensions (the tables cover the data). The list's caption is screen-reader-only.
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies and about 1,000 lines of app code for 25 records, with one dev dependency (playwright-core). The collision-search label packer (drawing.js:207-240) is the most complex part. It is justified by the 'no overlap' requirement, but it is heavy.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers run, addresses, the file map, tests and drawing decisions, and docs/testing.md explains the e2e setup. There is a package-lock and the regression tests are broad. Missing: no CI configuration, no engines field or .nvmrc for Node 22, and the dependency is a caret range ('^1.64.1'). There is no release or versioning approach beyond '1.0.0'. Design decisions and the spec exist only in app/.worktrees/cip-cartridge-reference/docs/superpowers/ — a gitignored duplicate worktree, including a .git file and .opencode config, shipped inside the app folder. The main tree has no ADRs or specs. The README says the Chromium setup needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH tweaks, which is a manual step.
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent: a system font with uppercase small headings, monospace symbols and tabular numbers. The single blue accent is used for links, the button and dimensions, and borders are restrained. The drawing looks like a clean technical drawing, with blue dimensions, black outline, fine hatching and a grey bullet section (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). The title block is heavy, oversized relative to the drawing and wider than the part. The pages look consistent and finished.
evidence.layout: Structure: toolbar, h1, a facts grid, the drawing, cartridge tables, chamber tables, then the source footer. The most important content comes first and nothing overlaps or clips in any screenshot. The facts grid wraps the water-capacity note into a narrow tall column, which leaves gaps (detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing panel wastes horizontal space on desktop. The print packs the tables into four columns and fits one page.
evidence.usability: Search filters as the user types and also matches alternative names, with commas and points treated alike. Family combines with search, and the filter state is kept when going back. Each name is a link straight to its detail view, and the detail view offers a clear Print button and an 'All cartridges' link. Unknown keys show a not-found page with a link back. The list cannot be sorted. '1 cartridges' is literal to the brief but reads awkwardly.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would find it trustworthy: values are as published, tolerances sit inline, and the drawings are true to scale and recognisable against the OpenBallistics references, with a section view and notes on missing values. The print sheet is useful. Engineers will notice that the shoulder angle has no proper angle dimension and that the drawing is fairly small on desktop and in print.

unmet_requirements: Shoulder angle α is drawn with a single-arrow leader and label only (drawing.js:242-247), not as a dimension with extension lines and arrowheads
Printed drawing is not at full width: max-height 140mm (style.css:155) shrinks the 308 Win. outline to about 75% of the page width (print-308_win.jpg)
Title block scale is only the A4 print scale; there is no scale for the on-screen view
strengths: The geometry implements every drawing rule faithfully, including the chamfer, the groove, the belt ramp at δ, the rimfire half-round, the shoulder fillets, the tangent ogive, the heeled bullet, walls and primer pocket. Drawings are true to scale against the reference drawings, and missing values are listed under the drawing.

Labels do not overlap: a collision search places them, and this is verified for all 25 records both in unit tests and in Chromium with real font metrics. Each detail view prints on one A4 page, black on white.
Thorough tests: unit tests per rule and record, plus e2e coverage of search, filter, routing, reload, phone width, dark mode, no network requests, and printing every record on one A4 page.
issues: The shoulder angle α has only a leader with a label, not an angle dimension with extension lines as the brief asks for every dimension.

The drawing is undersized for its space: on desktop, 80vh caps its height and leaves wide empty margins; in print, max-height 140mm keeps it below full width and leaves blank space at the bottom of the page.
Repository hygiene and maintainability: no CI, no Node version pin, a caret dev-dependency range, and the design spec exists only in a duplicate .worktrees copy shipped inside app/.
review.verdict: The app is a solid, dependency-free reference whose drawings follow the brief's geometry rules closely, stay true to scale and print cleanly on one A4 page, and it is backed by unusually thorough tests. To publish it with confidence, the shoulder angle needs a proper angle dimension, the drawing should use the available width on screen and in print, and the repository needs cleanup and a CI pipeline.
